hero.lede: Small-batch Indian coffee from Bengaluru. We roast twelve kilos every Tuesday, before the city wakes up. Reserve a bag from the next one.

coffees.name: Araku Dawn
coffees.description: Bright and clean. The one to drink black, on its own, while it is still dark outside.

coffees.name: Baba Budan
coffees.description: Dried in the fruit, so it tastes like it. Loud, jammy and hard to put down.

coffees.name: Nilgiri Mist
coffees.description: Grown between tea gardens and it shows. Gentle enough for a second cup, and a third.

coffees.name: Malabar Monsoon
coffees.description: Aged in monsoon winds until the beans swell and the acidity disappears. Built for filter kaapi with milk.

steps.title: Roast
steps.body: Twelve kilos, one coffee at a time, while the street is empty and nobody can smell it.

steps.title: Taste
steps.body: We cup every batch. Anything that misses its profile becomes staff coffee.

steps.title: Pack
steps.body: Each bag is sealed by hand, with the roast date printed on the front.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.body: Delivered anywhere in India, rested just enough to brew well the day it lands.

story.title: Why so early
paragraphs: Odd Hour started in 2019 with a one-kilo sample roaster in a Malleshwaram garage. The neighbours complained about the smoke every afternoon.
So we tried roasting at 4 a.m. Nobody has complained since. We kept the hour, and we kept the batches small enough to taste every one.
